title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Program Year's Emergency Dispatches
content:
Each emergency or critical dispatch under the Demand Service Rate Programs consumes one of the program year's included emergency calls.

The clause below is no longer in force, and a dispatch beyond the included calls is not priced by it
today:

> A call taken once the year's included calls are used up still runs at the tier's emergency response guarantee, and it carries the tier's emergency surcharge on top of the labor and parts of the call.

The count is taken over the current program year only and it counts dispatches, not work orders, so a
single fault that brings the technician back a second time on the same night counts twice unless the
second trip is a callback. At the top tier, where the surcharge is zero, the count is still kept because
it drives the year-end service review. A call the office itself reclassifies downward after arrival is
released back to the allowance and the surcharge, where it was applied, is credited.

| What happened on the program | Effect on the program year's allowance |
|---|---|
| an emergency dispatch is taken | one included emergency call is consumed |
| a critical dispatch is taken | one included emergency call is consumed |
| the technician returns the same night on a new dispatch for the same fault | a second call is consumed |
| that return trip is a callback | no further call is consumed |
| the office reclassifies the call downward after arrival | the call is released back to the allowance, and the surcharge, where it was applied, is credited |

*Why the count is kept at the top tier.* At the Dedicated Technician Program the surcharge stands at
zero, and the count is kept because it drives the year-end service review.
